versions.changelog: Markets: tick several markets and load them together (a station in more than one appears once; the main market sets the coverage center and the time zone for newscast times). Save your current stations and teams as a market of your own, import or export market files, delete your own markets and hide bundled ones.

Station logos in Live TV and the guide for all 30 bundled stations. Stations that stream only during newscasts (KOAT, KGWN) list their newscasts in the guide at their times, with "Not streaming" between them. Stations set up by an earlier version get their logos and newscast times automatically.

Keep streams ready fixes: the background warm-up runs one station at a time and always leaves room for someone tuning in or a local game; stations whose stream links expire within minutes are renewed at most every 10 minutes; a station edited while it was being warmed is tried with its new settings right away; turning the setting on or off no longer refreshes the guide. Signed-in stations check only the page itself (not embedded widgets) for a sign-in prompt before signing in again.

Keep streams ready: a new setting has the sidecar find every enabled station's stream ahead of time and renew it in the background, so tuning in is instant instead of taking 15 to 20 seconds. A station with nothing to play is checked less and less often. KOAT 7 streams its newscasts from its NowCast page, and ION (KPXC) plays ION's national feed from its free Pluto TV channel (19 stations enabled; use "Load this market's stations and teams" to pick them up). Setup steps for Windows (PowerShell) and macOS in the README.

Station sign-ins: for a station that streams only to signed-in (free) accounts, save the account in the station's settings, or have the account created for you when the site's sign-up form asks only for an email and password. The sidecar keeps it encrypted, signs in through the site's form, and stops at a CAPTCHA. Any confirmation email is yours to open.

Estrella TV (KETD) streams again from its new live page (17 stations enabled; use "Load this market's stations and teams" to pick it up). A station with nothing to play right now, such as one that streams only during its newscasts, shows a "Nothing is streaming right now" screen instead of a playback error. Test now names a bot check when a site shows one. Team schedules that fail to load (after a restart, say) are retried within minutes instead of half an hour.

Coverage area: set a maximum distance and your location (or use this device's location) to keep only nearby stations in Live TV; each station's city and distance show in the settings. Stations set up by an earlier version get their locations automatically. KWGN CW2, KDVR FOX31 and KXRM FOX21 stream again (16 stations enabled); use "Load this market's stations and teams" to turn them on.

Channels added or removed while Jellyfin was down (for example by upgrading the plugin) now show up in Live TV on their own: the first sync after a restart refreshes the guide when the station list changed, instead of waiting for Sync now or the daily guide refresh.

Wider coverage: the Denver market now reaches every TV market covering part of Colorado plus Cheyenne (30 stations, 13 enabled, up from 6), including Gray Television stations such as KKTV 11, whose streams now play (also behind DNS ad blockers). Local games prefer Denver stations. Use "Load this market's stations and teams" in the settings to get the new stations.

Bug fixes: streams no longer stall at each refresh, a failed Test leaves a playing channel alone, sturdier settings page (clear errors for a wrong sidecar URL or API key), Local Sports guide starts with the pre-game, and better stream detection on station pages.

name: Local Broadcast
overview: Local TV stations' free web streams in Live TV, local sports first
description: Adds your market's local TV stations to Live TV as an M3U tuner with a guide, using the free live streams on the stations' own websites (found by the local-broadcast sidecar, a small Docker container). Stations airing a local team's game come first, and a Local Sports channel always plays the station that has the game.
